function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you pull the telemetry data for the node at 23.31.32.1 in the **test‑de** fabric.  
To do that with the `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get` function, I’ll need a few more details:

| What you need to provide | Why it matters |
|--------------------------|----------------|
| **nodeId** (numeric) – the internal ID that maps to the IP 23.31.32.1 | The function requires a numeric node identifier, not an IP address. |
| **podId** (numeric) – the pod that contains the node | Telemetry data is scoped to a specific pod. |
| **interfaceType** (`"svi" | "ethernet" | "loopback" | "port-channel"`) | Which type of interface you’re interested in. |
| **infoType** (`"interfaces" | "status" | "statistics" | "errors"`) | The kind of information you want returned. |

Once you have those values, you can call the function like this (in Python syntax):

```python
from functions import telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get

result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get(
    fabricName="test-de",
    nodeId=<NODE_ID>,          # replace with the numeric ID for 23.31.32.1
    podId=<POD_ID>,            # replace with the pod ID
    interfaceType="ethernet",  # or whichever type you need
    infoType="interfaces"      # or "status", "statistics", etc.
)

print(result)
```

If you’re not sure what the node ID or pod ID is for that IP, let me know and I can walk you through how to look it up (e.g., via your inventory or a lookup API). Once we have those numbers, the call above will return the requested telemetry data.
